_about: Rules learned from the owner's edits in the Construction lab. The lab drafts with them, the Trace study shows them beside every sign, and GPT/Codex read them here. Add a rule when an edit teaches one.

kradin.rule: Bars sit exactly on an axis: base 49, mid 350, top 651 (at Black).
Continue an existing stroke end (extension) rather than adding a new stroke: hya, hye, hyi, za, vɛ, vi, ma, mɛ, ba, bu.
A modifier bar starts at the rightmost element's crossing and runs about 120 past the sign; tighter spacing is fine.
kp / gb bracket: one stroke at the top axis, L40, quarter turn r100, straight down, quarter turn r100, L40 (longer tail allowed); for o, ɛ, ɔ it hangs from mid height.
kradin.from: kpa, kpe, kpi, kpo, kpɔ, kpu, gba..gbu, 28 Oct

kradin.rule: y glide: a small loop on the left that comes down as a stem to the baseline (ya). Drawn for ye..yu from ya.
w glide: a bar along the top axis running left from the vowel and ending in a curl under itself (wa). Drawn for we..wu from wa.
When a composite needs it, unlock and redraw it as one sign (gu, ya, kwa, kwe) instead of forcing the parts.
Stay close to the original Koradin over strict clearance; free angles are accepted.

Koradin.otf is the immutable reference; interpret strokes and reusable components, not every junction as a new shape; preserve vertical and horizontal supports; mirrored counterparts come from one base.
The comma is one closed stroke: a square with concave sides and four points, after the original.

latin.rule: Every glyph sits exactly on the baseline, x-height and cap height (points within 14 units are snapped).
Near-vertical stem ends at an alignment line run straight on and are cut flat on it; the foot width is measured on the line.
Outlines: nodes only at extrema and corners, horizontal/vertical handles at extrema, integer coordinates, no overlaps.
Modular Latin fonts take the weight axis only, no style presets.

Each letter has a stroke plan (a = bowl + stem, n = stem + arch, M = up to 4 strokes; see PLAN in src/autotrace.py). The tracer prefers readings that match it and splits a letter at its sharpest corner when it has too few strokes.
Straight upright stems of the same case share one middle weight across the font; their ends keep their own flare or taper.
